title: Settings not synced between elevated and non-levated runs; configs reset after restart / update
next_action: Wait for same-account before/after settings evidence; no competing fix should start.

judgment.rationale: The attached report shows elevated and non-elevated activity but only a final settings snapshot. It cannot distinguish a same-account persistence failure from expected settings separation after elevating with another Windows account.
evidence: Reporter supplied a diagnostic archive after triage requested it.
The archive records is_elevated=true and run_elevated=true.
The runner log contains a non-elevated start before later settings activity.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the account relationship and a controlled before/after comparison using the same Windows account.

fix_assessment.rationale: A repository fix cannot be responsibly scoped until expected per-user isolation is separated from a same-account settings persistence defect.

issue_context.summary: Settings appear different after switching between non-elevated and elevated PowerToys sessions, but the diagnostic does not establish whether the sessions used the same Windows profile.
known_information: FancyZones, Keyboard Manager, and PowerToys Run are cited as affected.
The diagnostic contains elevated and non-elevated activity.
The final settings snapshot has is_elevated=true and run_elevated=true.
inferences: Using a different administrator account would legitimately use a different per-user configuration.
A same-account reproduction could still reveal a settings-path or persistence defect.
issue_context.analysis: The new diagnostic resolves the missing-log request but not the decisive account and before/after state questions. A code change now could incorrectly merge configurations across Windows users.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, comments, labels, attachment reference, and linked issue activity.
Reviewed runner elevation selection and settings-window behavior.
No linked upstream PR or concrete fix attempt covers this issue.

information_gaps.information: Whether the UAC prompt used the same Windows account that originally configured PowerToys.
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates expected per-user settings isolation from a defect.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the account relationship without naming the accounts.

information_gaps.information: One visible non-default setting recorded before and after Restart as administrator and one reboot, with is_elevated and run_elevated values.
information_gaps.why_needed: Identifies whether the value changes at elevation, startup, or update.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Use the same account, record the values, and add `/bugreport` immediately after a failing transition.

comment.body:
Thanks for the report. To resolve the recorded uncertainty, please provide:

1. Whether the UAC prompt used the same Windows account that originally configured PowerToys. Collection: Confirm the account relationship without naming the accounts.
2. One visible non-default setting recorded before and after Restart as administrator and one reboot, with is_elevated and run_elevated values. Collection: Use the same account, record the values, and add `/bugreport` immediately after a failing transition.
